prompt: Build a marketing landing page in a new .pen document at 1440x900 with three regions: (1) a top hero section with a centered headline, subhead, and a primary CTA button; (2) a three-column features section below the hero, each column with an icon, a heading, and one paragraph of body text; (3) a footer with a copyright line and three text links. Use placeholder copy. Aim for clean spacing rhythm and consistent typography. Build it incrementally region by region and after each region tell me what you verified and how you verified it (which MCP tools, in what order, with which nodeId). At the end, give me a one-paragraph summary of the total verification calls you made across the whole build, broken down by tool type.
expected_output: Agent builds the page in 3+ batch_design chunks (one per region, possibly more for dense regions). Verification across the whole build follows the four-rung ladder. Critical metric: total get_screenshot calls across the entire build is 1 or 2, NOT one per region. Most per-region verification is structural (snapshot_layout on the just-built region's parent frame, sometimes batch_get to confirm ref instantiation or property bindings). When get_screenshot is used, it is scoped to a specific nodeId (the region just built or the page root for final sign-off), never an unscoped call. The agent does NOT re-screenshot in dark mode. The closing paragraph reports the breakdown honestly; if the agent took more than 2 screenshots, it should say so rather than under-report. The pattern that distinguishes new-skill behavior from old-skill behavior is: structural-first verification per region, with screenshots reserved for the page-level final sign-off and any genuinely-visual question (e.g., did an AI image generate as expected). Old-skill behavior would screenshot after each region (3+ screenshots, typically full-page).
